indications: Indicated to reduce the risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and revascularization procedures in adults with multiple cardiovascular risk factors or established coronary heart disease. Indicated as an adjunct to diet for reduction of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides, and to increase HDL-C in hyperlipidemia and mixed dyslipidemia.
dosage_and_administration: Adults: Starting dose is 10 mg to 20 mg orally once daily. Patients requiring large LDL-C reductions (> 45%) may start at 40 mg once daily. Maintenance dose range is 10 mg to 80 mg once daily. Administer as a single dose at any time of day, with or without food. Assess lipid levels within 2 to 4 weeks following initiation or titration and adjust dosage accordingly.
contraindications: Active liver disease, including unexplained persistent elevations in hepatic transaminase levels. Pregnancy and breastfeeding (cholesterol is essential for fetal development; statins may cause fetal harm). Hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any component of the medication.
drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (Clarithromycin, Itraconazole, Ketoconazole, HIV protease inhibitors) dramatically increase atorvastatin systemic exposure, multiplying myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk. Consuming large quantities of Grapefruit Juice (> 1.2 liters daily or concentrated grapefruit extract) inhibits intestinal CYP3A4 and markedly increases atorvastatin plasma levels. Concomitant Fibrates (especially Gemfibrozil) or Cyclosporine substantially escalates rhabdomyolysis risk. Digoxin serum levels may increase slightly when taken with atorvastatin.
side_effects: Common: Nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, pain in extremity, urinary tract infection, and mild dyspepsia. Infrequent: Elevation in serum transaminases (ALT/AST), mild elevation in HbA1c/fasting serum glucose. Serious: Rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure secondary to myoglobinuria, and immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM).
critical_warnings: RHABDOMYOLYSIS AND MYOPATHY WARNING: Patients should be instructed to immediately report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, particularly if accompanied by malaise, fever, or dark (tea-colored) urine. Severe rhabdomyolysis can lead to acute renal failure and death. Atorvastatin therapy must be discontinued immediately if markedly elevated creatine kinase (CK) levels occur or if myopathy is diagnosed or suspected.
